item.text:
## Ranked proposals

**1. A small Tide Lines table display using Mara’s captions and field notes**  
Use the three recorded water observations alongside Mara’s caption drafts to make a modest educational display about how water levels can change familiar routes. The observation log is explicitly a written field note, not a scientific dataset, so present it as personal observations rather than scientific evidence. Mara permits reuse of her written notes and captions in free public educational displays. [observations.txt](/tmp/work/01-projects/tide-lines/observations.txt), [text-fragments.txt](/tmp/work/01-projects/tide-lines/text-fragments.txt), [tide-notes.txt](/tmp/work/03-rights/tide-notes.txt)

The library says a free table display may be possible next month, subject to confirming dates; it is not booked. Mara has one weekend, and a twelve-page black-and-white print run is quoted at $8, within the $30 cap. The studio printer may not be available on the day, and the quote expires next month. [venue.txt](/tmp/work/04-resources/venue.txt), [request.txt](/tmp/work/04-resources/request.txt), [printing-quote.txt](/tmp/work/04-resources/printing-quote.txt), [printing.txt](/tmp/work/02-assets/notes/printing.txt)

**Next step:** Confirm a date with library staff and printer availability. Draft a short display using only Mara’s text and notes. Do not include photos or S-3: the photos require separate written photographer consent, and S-3 is absent from the archive with ownership and public-use permission unconfirmed. [photo-terms.txt](/tmp/work/03-rights/photo-terms.txt), [sound-index.txt](/tmp/work/02-assets/notes/sound-index.txt), [sound-terms.txt](/tmp/work/03-rights/sound-terms.txt)

**2. A hands-on Folded Water paper demonstration, conditional on written collaborator permission**  
The workshop notes describe paper cutouts that cast bands of light when moved, and the materials record says the prototype used card, blue offcuts, and scissors. A small demonstration could explain how a repeated shape represents a changing shoreline without a projector. [workshop.txt](/tmp/work/01-projects/folded-water/workshop.txt), [materials.txt](/tmp/work/01-projects/folded-water/materials.txt), [demo-notes.txt](/tmp/work/01-projects/folded-water/demo-notes.txt)

However, the maker agreement bars public display or adaptation of FW-7 unless the collaborator separately grants written permission; no such agreement is recorded. The shelf inventory is from 2 October and must be checked before production. [folded-water.txt](/tmp/work/03-rights/folded-water.txt), [craft-box.txt](/tmp/work/02-assets/notes/craft-box.txt)

**Next step:** Ask the collaborator for written permission before displaying or adapting FW-7, and check current supplies. There is also an unresolved version discrepancy: the diagram and later workshop record specify three slits, while an earlier draft says two, with no final-authoritative signoff. [shape-diagram.txt](/tmp/work/01-projects/folded-water/shape-diagram.txt), [old-copy.txt](/tmp/work/02-assets/notes/old-copy.txt)

**3. Hypothesis: a text-only Tide Lines route-change display with verified historical context**  
The idea could pair Mara’s permitted captions and observations with a carefully verified statement about the inlet path moving inland in 1981. The archive’s library note says to verify that historical statement against the original reference before publishing; it does not supply that reference. [concept.txt](/tmp/work/01-projects/tide-lines/concept.txt), [research.txt](/tmp/work/01-projects/tide-lines/research.txt), [tide-notes.txt](/tmp/work/03-rights/tide-notes.txt)

This is a possibility, not yet a ready proposal: verify the source before using the historical claim. Keep the photos out unless separate written photographer consent is obtained. [photos-index.txt](/tmp/work/01-projects/tide-lines/photos-index.txt), [photo-terms.txt](/tmp/work/03-rights/photo-terms.txt)

## Scope and uncertainties

I inventoried and read the files returned by a workspace file listing. The archive is primarily text; referenced photo files and sound recording S-3 are not present. This supports a small, low-cost text display as the most immediately feasible idea, but does not establish that the archive contains every relevant record or that the printer, craft supplies, or library date will be available. No blanket rights are recorded for third-party contributions. [general.txt](/tmp/work/03-rights/general.txt)
